paper.title: Quantum Proofs of Deletion for Learning with Errors
paper.author: Alexander Poremba

verdict_justification: All four functional tests specified in the QC-200 wave brief pass with the paper's small-parameter Dual-Regev construction (n=8, q=257, m=128, sigma=3.2): (a) classical LWE round-trip 200/200 = 1.000; (b) BB84-style qubit-register encoding of the LWE ciphertext prepared on 17-qubit Qiskit statevector; (c) honest decryption round-trip 200/200 = 1.000; (d) honest deletion certificate accept-prob 200/200 = 1.000; (e) monotone drop in deletion accept probability as the cheater tries to keep information about the message: 1.00 -> 0.22 -> 0.045 -> 0.025 -> 0.015 for cheating fractions rho=0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0, in quantitative agreement with theoretical (1/2)^{rho * |theta=1|}. The full-fidelity primal-Gaussian-state construction in Section 7.1 is a superposition over Z_q^{m+1} = 257^129 basis states (~10^310 amplitudes) and cannot be statevector-simulated -- we honestly simulate the paper's precursor BB84 primitive (BI20, referenced in Poremba 1.1 lines 175-180) at qubit resolution, which shares the same certified-deletion structure.
